text: The fuel is uranium, packed into long rods. When a uranium atom splits, it releases heat, and a few neutrons that can split more atoms. A chain reaction. Those neutrons work best when they're slowed down. In an R B M K, that's done by a huge stack of graphite blocks. Water is pumped up through more than a thousand channels in the graphite. It boils, and the steam spins turbines that make electricity. To control it all, rods of boron, which swallows neutrons, slide in and out from above.
